description:
git::sync::tests::migrate_store_ref_to_v2_dry_run_peeks_remote_without_mutating_tracking_ref fails at crates/kopi-beans/src/git/sync.rs:3279.

  assertion `left == right` failed
    left: OrSetV1
   right: LegacyEdges

PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the network-push change in f06e642 -- verified by stashing that change and re-running on a clean tree at 77410f2, where it fails identically. Rest of the git suite is green (130 passed, 1 failed, 4 ignored).

The test builds its own temp local/remote repos and writes a legacy-edges store commit, then asserts the dry run reports deps_format_before == LegacyEdges. It observes OrSetV1 instead, i.e. the dry run is reading a deps format that has already been converted. Worth checking whether write_store_commit_with_custom_deps is actually producing legacy edges, or whether migrate_store_ref_to_v2's peek path normalises before reporting.

Found while fixing the gix push gate.
title: gix_compat: migrate_store_ref_to_v2 dry-run test fails (OrSetV1 vs LegacyEdges)

description:
NEEDS THE MAINTAINER'S CALL -- deliberately not 'fixed' either way, because both sides are defensible and picking one is a product decision, not a test cleanup.

Found by the quality gate on the develop->main merge (merge touched zero kmux files -- pre-existing). This is the LAST kmux failure; the other 10 were stale rmux-branding assertions and are fixed (gh-74, gh-75).

THE CONFLICT

crates/kmux/tests/cli_surface.rs:2004 socket_path_flag_can_start_directly_under_tmp asserts kmux can start with a socket placed DIRECTLY in /tmp:
    -S /tmp/rmux-direct-socket-<pid>-cli-surface.sock

crates/kmux/src/sdk/bootstrap/startup_unix.rs:232 refuses exactly that:
    i/o error: kmux startup refused '/tmp': permissions 0o1777 grant access beyond the owner

The startup path has UnsafeOwner + UnsafePermissions checks that reject a socket parent directory which is not owner-only. /tmp is 1777 (world-writable, sticky) on every mainstream Unix, so this test fails for ANY user on Linux/macOS, not just in CI -- it is not environment-specific and not flaky.

WHY BOTH SIDES ARE DEFENSIBLE

* Keep the hardening: a world-writable socket directory invites a local attacker to pre-create or squat the socket path. Refusing it is a real mitigation and the checks look deliberately written, not accidental.
* Keep the compat: tmux itself happily accepts -S /tmp/foo.sock, and kmux's whole selling point is being a tmux-compatible drop-in. Refusing a path tmux accepts is a compatibility break that will surprise people porting scripts.

Plausible resolution (maintainer decides): allow an explicit user-supplied -S path to opt out of the parent-directory permission check while keeping the check for the DEFAULT socket location -- the default is kmux's choice and should be safe, but an explicit -S is the user overriding kmux's judgment knowingly. That preserves the mitigation where it matters and restores tmux compat where the user asked for it. Would need the test renamed/kept and a doc note.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, on purpose: did not weaken or bypass the security check to make a test pass, and did not skip/disable/quarantine the test (CLAUDE.md forbids both).
title: kmux: socket_path_flag_can_start_directly_under_tmp -- the /tmp hardening check and the tmux-compat test contradict each other
